steps.text: Season pork with taco seasoning. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork; cook until browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in salsa and peach preserves until combined.
Cover the skillet; reduce the heat. Simmer gently for about 10 minutes, then serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Peach Pork Picante
raw_recipe.description: This tasty one-skillet spicy-sweet pork picante recipe has the sweet and tangy flavors of peach preserves and salsa — it’s perfect for busy weeknights.
raw_recipe.name: Peach Pork Picante

review.reviewBody: I've been making this receipe for about 10 years. I have change it quite considerably. I used chicken cutlets (not a huge fan of pork) that I cut into small pieces. Two packs of salsa seasonings. Shake the chicken in bag w/ the seasonings and lightly brown chicken in skillet. I 'dump' 3 jars of salsa (Old el paso) into chicken and a whole jar of peach preserves. Let it simmer until hot - 10 min. I serve it w/ rice (or egg noodles) - I have more than enough sauce to spoon over the rice to serve as a side. It will feed about 6 people. Reheats excellently.

This dish is fantastic! I bought a jar of Newman's own peach salsa instead of combining regular salsa with fruit preserves and it came out delicious! Served with a side of black beans....will be making this one weekly!

This has quickly turned into one of my favorite dinner recipes. The easy to delicious ratio is fantastic. I like a little less salsa and a little more peach flavor, so I use 2/3 c. salsa and 5 tablespoons peach preserves. I also like to add a chopped green pepper to the mix for some added flavor and healthfulness.

I'd give this a 10. Simple and easy. I had taken out about 1 1/2 lbs of pork cubes from the freezer so I used the full package of Taco seasoning but needed some more which I didn't have on hand. I had some rib seasoning leftover from the week-end (1 tablespoon of cumin, 1 tablespoon chili powerder, 1 tablespoon of paprika) so I added that. It was perfect - right amount of heat! Since I was using more meat I did use 2 cups of salsa and 8 tablespoons of peach preserves. I served it over spanish rice. There were only the two of us and we had to stop ourselves from eating the entire serving. My guy already claimed the leftovers for lunch. Thanks submitter.

I've been making this recipe for over 30 years (got it out of a magazine). It has always been one of my favorites! I've tried it with pork, but it never seems to get tender enough for me so instead I used 2 large boneless chicken breasts. Tonight I added some extra items I had sitting around. I added about 15-20 Cherub tomatoes , and I started the recipe by adding a medium diced onion and a half of a diced red bell pepper in a couple of tablespoons of EVOO. When they were tender, I added the chicken and finished off the recipe. The additions put this recipe over the top! If you're not a fan of spicy, then you might opt for Mild Taco Mix. I served it with a fresh salad.

I originally saw this as a crockpot recipe but I’m glad that I cooked it on the stovetop. That way you can adjust your salsa, preserves, and seasoning to get a sweeter, spicier, or more tomato flavor based on your preference. My family doesn’t like pork, so I used chicken breast and served over steamed white rice with seasoned black beans on the side. It’s delicious and everyone cleaned their plates. I recommend doubling the sauce and letting the rice soak up all the saucy goodness. It takes 20 minutes on the stove. Great for a quick weeknight meal and no crockpot required.

Have made this twice for my family! everyone loves it! Used fresh peaches instead of peach preserves and made my own taco seasoning as we were out, used the recipe on this site, no salsa...so one can of rotel, one can of tomatoes, onions and lime juice. Yummy! you can even throw this in the croc pot and forget it!

this was So easy and very good, next time i might add some sugar snap peas to it, i used brown rice instead of white. i didn't use taco seasoning i just used garlic, onion and 1tsp of cumin and a tsp of salsa and some veg broth to get it started and then followed the recipie. still turned out really well!! thanks for posting it up here!

VERY easy meal to make; I didn't have peach preserves, so I mixed a can of peaches (with their juice) and 1/4 cup sugar in a sauce pan, brought it to a boil and let it reduce down, mashing the peaches as they cooked. Added a bit more than 4 Tablespoons of the peaches to the salsa mixture; made it all the more spicy sweet. I served it with black beans and rice. Between huge bites, my husband declared this was better than anything he's had in a restaurant. Thanks for helping to make me look so good!

Have made this twice for my family! everyone loves it! Used fresh peaches instead of peach preserves and made my own taco seasoning as we were out, used the recipe on this site, no salsa...so one can of rotel, one can of tomatoes, onions and lime juice. Yummy! you can even throw this in the croc pot and forget it!
This recipe is a new favorite of mine. I use it for chicken or pork and I add corn, black beans a little extra cumin with fresh cilantro on top and it is just fantastic!
I used Apricot preserves because I didn't have peach, but it was still wonderful!

I realize that the recipe shows no vegetables added; however, it really needs something other than just meat. It's too much meat! I had to make a salad to accommodate for the lack of vegetables. Granted this was very apparent from the recipe. As for the flavor, it is okay. I wouldn't say it is fabulous. I think if I was too make it again, I would eat it with a flour tortilla where I could add vegetables to it and have it as a well rounded meal.
Such a simple recipe, which I love, but also great flavor. Adding this to our regular menu rotation.
Too much taco seasoning and salsa, not enough peach. I couldn't even taste the peach. All I could taste was the taco seasoning
My granddaughter is always asking me to make this for her. We all love it.
Flavors galore! And in a good way. Perfect subtle sweetness with peach preserves. Used a can of Rotel since I don’t have salsa. Delish!
This is fast, tasty, makes great leftovers and everyone likes it. You can adjust the heat and sweetness easily. I serve it with white rice.
Very easy to make. I had my doubts about this, but this recipe is the most tender pork i've ever made. Very tasty and full of flavor!

I love this recipe. My Mom gave it to me about 20 years ago. I basically use pork stew meat or boneless pork chops cut into bite size. I have served it mainly over rice, but egg noodles are just as good. Since we like heat, I use hot salsa like Pace. This is a classic recipe that will never get old!
